label: Nouns — Society & State
description: A 20-question check on society and state nouns.

questions.prompt: What does «Государство помогает своим гражданам.» mean?
questions.explain: «Государство» is the nominative subject and «помогает своим гражданам» means it helps its citizens in the dative.

questions.prompt: How would you say «The court made a fair decision» in Russian?
questions.explain: The card uses «Суд принял справедливое решение.» with «суд» as the nominative subject of «принял».

questions.prompt: In «Армия управляется государством.», what case is «государством»?
questions.explain: «Государством» is instrumental, naming the agent in this passive construction (run by the state).

questions.prompt: What is the gender of «власть» as in «Власть в стране меняется медленно.»?
questions.explain: «Власть» is a feminine noun ending in -ь, used here in the nominative as the subject.

questions.prompt: Complete: «Без ___ общество не выживет.» (without laws)
questions.explain: The preposition «без» governs the genitive, so the genitive plural «законов» is required.

questions.prompt: What does «Народ ненавидит любую войну.» mean?
options: The people fear a new war.
questions.explain: «Войну» is the accusative object of «ненавидит» (hates), with «любую» agreeing in the feminine accusative.

questions.prompt: In «Мы наконец победили врага.», why is the form «врага» used?
options: It is genitive after a preposition.
It is dative after the verb.
It is animate masculine, so its accusative matches the genitive.
questions.explain: «Враг» is animate masculine, so its accusative object form «врага» matches the genitive.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses the genitive of absence with «победа»?
questions.explain: «Без победы» uses the genitive «победы» after «без» to express absence.

questions.prompt: What does «Полиция уже приехала на место.» mean?
options: The police are about to leave the scene.
We called the police at night.
The criminal was detained by the police.
The police have already arrived at the scene.
questions.explain: «Полиция» is the feminine nominative subject of «приехала», and «на место» marks the destination (the scene).

questions.prompt: Which case is «свободу» in «Они борются за свободу.»?
questions.explain: The preposition «за» here governs the accusative, giving «свободу» in the sense of fighting for something.

questions.prompt: How would you say «The government passed a new law» in Russian?
questions.explain: «Правительство приняло новый закон.» has neuter «правительство» as the nominative subject of «приняло».

questions.prompt: What is the nominative plural of «закон», as in «Эти ___ давно устарели.»?
questions.explain: «Законы» is the nominative plural with the masculine -ы ending, the subject of «устарели».

questions.prompt: What does «Преступник стал жертвой обстоятельств.» mean?
options: The criminal found the only victim.
The criminal became a victim of circumstances.
The victim was left without help.
The city remembers the victims of war.
questions.explain: «Жертвой» is instrumental after «стал» (became), with «обстоятельств» the genitive plural completing the idiom.

questions.prompt: Complete: «Они готовятся ___ войне.» (preparing for war)
questions.explain: The preposition «к» governs the dative «войне», expressing preparation toward something.

questions.prompt: Which case is «обществом» in «Интернет управляет современным обществом.»?
questions.explain: The verb «управлять» always takes the instrumental, so «обществом» is instrumental here.

questions.prompt: How would you say «We are proud of our team» in Russian?
questions.explain: «Я горжусь нашей командой.» uses instrumental «командой» because «гордиться» governs the instrumental.

questions.prompt: What does «У него было много врагов.» mean?
options: He did not trust his enemy.
questions.explain: «Много» requires the genitive plural «врагов», and «у него было» expresses past possession (he had).

questions.prompt: What is the gender of «революция» as in «Революция изменила всю страну.»?
questions.explain: «Революция» is feminine, shown by the agreeing feminine past-tense verb «изменила».

questions.prompt: Complete: «В Европе много небольших ___.» (small states)
questions.explain: After «много» the noun takes the genitive plural «государств», with «небольших» agreeing in the genitive plural.

questions.prompt: What does «Страна живёт под угрозой войны.» mean?
options: The country prevented a terrible threat.
There is no threat right now.
The country prepared for the threat of flooding.
The country lives under the threat of war.
questions.explain: «Под» here takes the instrumental «угрозой» (under threat), and «войны» is genitive naming the danger.
